Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

form noun

a shape

also shape, figure, outline, form (grammatical), grammatical form, female figure

classical

Cic. Fin. 5.35: tōtaque figūra et fōrma et statūra (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 318

1fōrma: long o (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 233–234, s.v. fōrma, prints the o long; Ernout–Meillet “stress the length of o”, which he takes for a recent lengthening of short o before r and a consonant (Leumann 1977: 114).

fōrma1, fōrmae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

form, shape, outward appearance

The shape of anything; of a person also beauty (fōrmā excellente, Liv. 1.9.11, Lewis & Short). A mould is a fōrma too (see baking tin).

Other words

  • figūra, figūrae f. — figure, shape; the form of a word

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 5.35 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 318: (of a word) figūra; Traupman 29: form (grammatical); Traupman 318 · Declension on Wiktionary

    From fingō, mould: the outline a thing has been given. In grammar the form of a word (Traupman 318; M-O s.v. form, grammatical).

Examples

  • nūdaque cōnsistunt, fōrmam servantia testae, vīna

    the wine stands bare, keeping the shape of its jarOv. Tr. 3.10.23–24

  • muliebris fōrma

    the female figureTraupman 314

  • Figūra est aut simplex, ut “doctus,” aut composita, ut “indoctus.”

    The form is either simple, like “doctus,” or compound, like “indoctus.”Traupman 318

  • Fac imperātīvum “venīre” verbī.

    Form the imperative of the verb “venīre”.Traupman 318

See also square, baking tin, form, design.
